{{short description|German-American chemist}}
'''Frank N. Keutsch''' (born 1971 in [[Tübingen]])<ref name=ACS>{{Cite web |title=ACS Fall 2010 Newsletter |url=http://phys-acs.org/archive/newsletters/F2010.html}}</ref> is a German-American chemist and a researcher on [[solar geoengineering]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tien Nguyen |date=2018-03-26 |title=Will the world ever be ready for solar geoengineering? |journal=C&EN Global Enterprise |language=en |volume=96 |issue=13 |pages=28–33 |doi=10.1021/cen-09613-cover |issn=2474-7408|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Engineering the Earth {{!}} Magazine {{!}} The Harvard Crimson |url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2019/3/7/keith-geoengineering/ |access-date=2022-12-23 |website=www.thecrimson.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Bojanowski |first=Axel |date=2021-11-01 |title=Klima: Mit künstlichen Wolken gegen den menschengemachten Klimawandel |language=de |work=DIE WELT |url=https://www.welt.de/wissenschaft/plus230439335/Solar-Engineering-Klima-Kuehlung-mit-kuenstlichen-Wolken-geplant.html |access-date=2022-12-23}}</ref> His research lies in [[atmospheric chemistry]], including the photochemical oxidation of [[Volatile organic compound|volatile organic compounds]] that lead to [[secondary organic aerosol]] formation. He leads the Stratospheric Controlled Perturbation Experiment ([[Stratospheric aerosol injection|SCoPEx]]) project at Harvard University with members including [[David Keith (physicist)|David Keith]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tollefson |first=Jeff |date=2018-11-27 |title=First sun-dimming experiment will test a way to cool Earth |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-018-07533-4 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=563 |issue=7733 |pages=613–615 |doi=10.1038/d41586-018-07533-4|pmid=30479388 |bibcode=2018Natur.563..613T |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Frank Keutsch |url=https://chemistry.harvard.edu/people/frank-keutsch |access-date=2022-12-23 |website=chemistry.harvard.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Keutsch was born in [[Tübingen]], Germany. He studied chemistry at the [[Technical University of Munich]] with a scholarship from the [[German National Academic Foundation]], receiving a diploma with Vladimir E. Bondybey. After graduating in 1997, Keutsch moved to the [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California at Berkeley]], where he received his Ph.D. in physical chemistry in 2001. His supervisor was [[Richard J. Saykally]] on high-resolution vibration-rotation-tunneling spectroscopy of [[Water cluster|water clusters]]. Keutsch then went to [[Harvard University]] as a postdoc, where he worked on stratospheric chemistry under the supervision of [[James G. Anderson]]. Keutsch began his independent academic career in 2005 as an assistant professor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]].<ref name=ACS></ref> He is currently the Stonington Professor in Engineering and Atmospheric Science at [[Harvard University]].

== Honors and awards ==
Keutsch won the following awards,<ref name=CV>{{Cite web |title=Frank Keutsch CV |url=https://www2.chem.wisc.edu/deptfiles/flyers/CV_Keutsch.DOC}}</ref>
* 2006 Camille and Henry Dreyfus Award Postdoctoral Program in Environmental Chemistry
* 2006 Favorite Instructor Fall 2006 from Ogg and Elizabeth Waters Halls
* 2005 Camille and Henry Dreyfus New Faculty Award
